description: SEBI passes a fresh order against Shri. Siddhant Suresh Chandan following SAT's remand directing re-computation of the fee liable to be refunded for providing unregistered investment advisory services.

title: SEBI Order in the Matter of Utilis Fund
description: SEBI passes an order in the matter of Utilis Fund, addressing regulatory compliance and enforcement actions related to the fund's operations.

title: Order in the Matter of Argentum Dynamic Alternative Investment Fund
description: SEBI enforcement order against Argentum Dynamic Alternative Investment Fund for violations of SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, with directions and/or penalties issued by the adjudicating authority.

title: SEBI Order: Market Access Restrained for 17 Entities in Veerkrupa Jewellers Matter
description: SEBI has restrained 17 individuals and entities from accessing the securities market for 3 to 5 years in connection with M/s Veerkrupa Jewellers Limited, via order dated May 29, 2026.

title: SEBI Order Against Suzlon Energy Limited for Financial Misrepresentation and PFUTP/LODR Violations
description: SEBI issues enforcement order under Section 15-I(3) of the SEBI Act and Section 23-I(3) of the SCRA against Suzlon Energy Limited and four officials for alleged misrepresentation in financial statements and violations of PFUTP and LODR Regulations during FY 2014-15 to FY 2020-21.

title: SEBI Order Against Mr. Nishaan Singh (Sanbun Investments) for Unregistered Portfolio Management Services
description: SEBI passes fresh order against Mr. Nishaan Singh, Proprietor of Sanbun Investments, following SAT remand to reassess quantum of funds received for unregistered portfolio management services and determine refund and debarment period.

title: SEBI Order Against Ventureland Asia Advisors Services LLP
description: SEBI enforcement order against Ventureland Asia Advisors Services LLP for violations of securities laws and regulations governing investment advisory or portfolio management services.

title: Order in the Matter of IndoStar Credit Fund
description: SEBI enforcement order dated May 22, 2026 in the matter of IndoStar Credit Fund, addressing regulatory compliance issues related to the fund's operations.

title: SEBI Order in the Matter of Domus Capital LLP
description: SEBI enforcement order against Domus Capital LLP for violations of securities laws, directing specific penalties or remedial actions as determined by the adjudicating authority.

title: SEBI Order in the Matter of India Electronic Development Fund
description: SEBI enforcement order concerning the India Electronic Development Fund (IEDF), an SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Fund focused on the electronics and semiconductor sector.

title: SEBI Order in the Matter of Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar Limited - Fund Diversion and RPT Non-Disclosure
description: SEBI order pursuant to Bombay High Court directions concerning Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar Limited, its promoters Shishir Bajaj and Kushagra Bajaj, involving alleged diversion of over ₹1,189 crore and non-disclosure of related party transactions.

title: SEBI Order Against Future Retail Limited Directors for Fraud, Misleading Disclosures and Fund Diversion
description: SEBI passes a 222-page enforcement order against 11 noticees including Kishore Biyani and other top executives of Future Retail Limited for misleading disclosures, understatement of debt, non-disclosure of related party transactions, and diversion of company funds.

title: SEBI Order on Front Running by Prijesh Kurani and Others
description: SEBI issued an enforcement order against 7 noticees including Prijesh Kurani and associates for front running trades of big client Anustup Trading Private Limited during January 2022 to February 2023.

title: SEBI Order Against Unregistered Investment Advisors Running Telegram Channels Intraday Jackpot and Professional Day Trading Institute
description: SEBI issues enforcement order against Akshay Kumar and five others for operating unregistered investment advisory and research analyst services through Telegram channels, collecting fees and making fraudulent profit claims.

title: Order Against M/s AFCO Capital India Private Limited - Merchant Banker Restrictions
description: SEBI issues order against AFCO Capital India Private Limited (SEBI Reg. No. INM000012555) for violations of Merchant Bankers Regulations, Intermediaries Regulations, PFUTP and PIT Regulations following inspection for April 2022 to August 2024.

title: Order in the matter of Front-running trades of Big Client - Sarvottam Securities Private Limited by multiple entities
description: SEBI order against four individuals — Mr. Sunny Bhatia, Mrs. Surbhi Chopra Bhatia, Mrs. Mamta Rani, and Mr. Kumar Ashok — for front-running trades of Big Client Sarvottam Securities Pvt. Ltd. in equity derivatives during January 2018 to December 2022.

title: SEBI Order Against Retro Green Revolution Limited - Price Manipulation and Market Fraud
description: SEBI issues enforcement order against 21 noticees including promoters and associates of Retro Green Revolution Limited for price manipulation, volume creation, and fraudulent trading activities on BSE.

title: Order Against Cash Cow Broking & Advisory Solutions for Unregistered Investment Advisory Activities
description: SEBI passes directions against Cash Cow Broking & Advisory Solutions and its partners for conducting investment advisory services without registration, ordering refund of fees collected from investors.

title: SEBI Order Against Arcotech Limited: Fund Diversion and Financial Statement Misrepresentation
description: SEBI issues enforcement order against Arcotech Limited and 13 related entities for alleged fund diversion of Rs.14.15 crores, fictitious transactions, and misrepresentation of financial statements across FY 2016-17 to 2020-21.

title: SEBI Order Against Mediaone Global Entertainment Ltd. for Fund Diversion and Financial Manipulation
description: SEBI issues enforcement order against Mediaone Global Entertainment Ltd. and its directors for alleged fund diversion and financial irregularities linked to Eros International Media Limited, involving a write-off of ₹63.61 crore.

title: Order in the matter of trading activities of certain entities in the scrip of DU Digital Technologies Limited (now DU Digital Global Limited)
description: SEBI order against 27 entities for employing deceptive trading strategies and contributing to artificial price and volume manipulation in DU Digital scrip during August 26, 2021 to March 31, 2023.

title: SEBI Final Order against M/s. MAN Industries (India) Limited and Others
description: SEBI final order regarding financial misrepresentation, non-consolidation of subsidiaries, and related party transaction non-disclosures by MAN Industries (India) Limited.

title: Final Order in the matter of Seacoast Shipping Services Limited
description: SEBI issued a final order under sections 11 and 11B of the SEBI Act, 1992 regarding Seacoast Shipping Services Limited and associated noticees concerning misrepresentation of financial statements and other violations.

title: Rajesh Shukla: Why do Indians travel within the country? Leisure is only a small part of the answer
description: Tourism within the country is shaped as much by faith, family and health as by leisure. In fact, each segment differs significantly in its spending, which has major implications for all those looking to make the most of this market opportunity.

title: Why it’s time for the US to ensure that everyone in America is covered by public health insurance
description: Premiums in the country are surging to unaffordable heights and this trend will only distort the labour market further. The answer to every hard question on cost, coverage, negotiation and market distortion lies is in universalizing health insurance.

title: What’s holding back private capital expenditure? The weakness of India’s unlisted corporate sector
description: While the financial position of the listed sector has improved post covid, that of the unlisted sector has worsened. This has constrained overall corporate investment in the Indian economy, given the size of the latter. Here's what the data record shows.

title: Oracles of AI are gambling with the future of children, workers and others. Why let them?
description: With technologists saying math need not be learnt now that we have AI at hand, it's clear that the cognitive skills of children are at peril. A hollowing out of human jobs is likely too. But AI spin-masters refuse to see the obvious.

title: Microsoft AI CEO: Humanity's choices on AI today will shape the future—we mustn't sleepwalk into it
description: While unanimity on how to regulate and develop AI may not be possible, let’s aim for a consensus on at least four points. This is crucial to ensure that humanity does not make decisions it comes to regret.

title: MSMEs and startups: converging for growth
description: As the boundaries between innovation, scale and production blur, India needs an ecosystem that combines the strengths of startups and traditional businesses.

title: India’s liquidity upswell: What should the central bank’s monetary policy committee do?
description: The Reserve Bank of India and its monetary policy committee have reason to worry about India’s macro complexities. As a policy meeting looms, a surge in liquidity should have the central bank anxious about its near-term effects. Will it act?

title: Mint Quick Edit | Tata's three-way merger idea may or may not work out—but it reflects the owner’s will
description: Have Tata Trusts found a way not to list Tata Sons? Awkward as their amalgamation plan sounds and regardless of how steep that path looks, a listing must not be forced upon the Tata Group’s holding company.

title: Rare diseases can be treated with tailored gene therapy but India’s regulatory system must evolve
description: India should review its regulation of new therapeutic paths enabled by tech advances. Think of AI and the wonders of Crispr gene editing. Safe ways exist to test modern therapies in a country that’s well placed to make breakthroughs.

title: The future of money: Why the West and China are betting on banks over Big Tech to lead the way
description: Attention is shifting from dollar clones like stablecoins to tokenized deposits, which are standard bank liabilities whose transfers can be executed with algorithms. Here's how programmable bank money could dominate global transactions.

title: Kaushik Basu: Is an AI-pocalypse inevitable? Not if we curb Big Tech’s concentrations of wealth
description: Amid an accelerating AI race between the US and China, fears of rogue bots and anxiety over human extinction, attention has shifted to what the tech may do to us rather than for us. A tax policy that reduces concentrations of financial clout would limit the risk of AI being deployed for a power grab

title: Managed rivalry: The world’s top two powers have made a move on mutual risk reduction
description: Last week, Washington and Beijing showed that they are capable of compartmentalizing their differences, even as the larger structural contest over technology, trade, security and regional influence persists. For India and the international system, adapting to that new equilibrium will be key.

title: RBI’s capital cushion tweak: Tighter norms don’t relieve banks of their need to track market risks
description: The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) latest directions will require prudential cushions to expand but banks mustn’t let their internal risk management slacken. The comfort of an extra capital buffer may prove pointless if lenders leave safety to regulation.

title: Fierce AI rivalry to become everyone’s agent-in-chief could reshape e-commerce beyond recognition
description: Amazon’s barring of Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is a flashpoint in an online battle that’s likely to erupt as agents vie to shop and spend money on behalf of humans. Businesses must stay alert. So must antitrust watchdogs.

title: Mint Quick Edit | Indian stocks near a six-month low: will domestic investors stay invested?
description: Rising oil prices and US bond yields have taken a toll on the Indian stock market, although corporate earnings have held up in a war-torn year. One trend to track is local investor money leaving our shores in search of better returns.

title: How a central bank digital currency helps governments in India meet their welfare promises
description: Uttarakhand has emerged as a pioneer state in its use of programmable money, the Reserve Bank of India’s e-rupee, to meet welfare commitments. Here's a case study of the key role played by India’s digital currency in agriculture.

title: China's auto industry is plagued with overcapacity—but a new deal could show the way out
description: The country's auto market has matured in recent years, with domestic sales slowing and factories running well below capacity. However, Toyota's new deal with its Chinese partners may help the industry gradually shrink.

title: Exam fraud in India: It’s a shape-shifting monster that finds new ways to prey on the vulnerable
description: A study of this illicit activity’s expansion reveals a variety of methods and a reach that extends to tubewell operator tests. It reveals a vast effort to prey on desperation, wherever it is found. That should make us squirm.

title: Principles of regulation must never be forgotten: Here are five deviations that India must fix right away
description: India is not ignorant of the canons of regulation. However, in insurance and many other sectors, regulators must abandon old habits of ignoring principles for Indian policy to spur economic growth instead of holding it back.

title: PM crop insurance enrolment rises as weather risks mount, Bengal rejoins scheme
description: PMFBY covered 27.3 million farmers in the 2026 Kharif season, with West Bengal’s return and concerns over monsoon risks driving wider participation.

title: IRDAI's new insurance rules proposal: Profits built on tears of policyholders are bad for country, says Monika Halan
description: Author Monika Halan thinks the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India's latest proposed regulatory overhaul in transition period offers insurers too much leeway to delay critical consumer protection measures.

title: Mint Explainer | What potential commission caps could mean for insurers
description: Irdai could set different commission ceilings for individual agents, agencies and bank-led distribution, while shifting compensation away from large upfront payouts.

title: Axis Max Life sees no immediate trigger for premium hikes, bets on small towns
description: Axis Max Life CEO Sumit Madan says India's insurance industry is having a “reasonably good run” despite global uncertainties.

title: Mint Explainer | Public insurance registry: how Irdai wants to build a digital backbone for insurance
description: Irdai's proposed registry could link policy, claims and risk data across insurers while connecting insurance with lenders, identity systems and public databases.

title: Insurance agents, brokers may get lower commission after GST cuts
description: Following the GST cut on insurance policies, insurers may reduce commissions for intermediaries to manage increased costs. With competitive pressures and regulatory caps, companies are seeking digital partnerships and expense rationalization to sustain growth while passing benefits to customers.

title: Bima Sugam India Federation website launch: IRDAI Chairman says ‘milestone’ for insurance sector — all you need to know
description: IRDAI has launched Bima Sugam, a digital platform aimed at creating a comprehensive Digital Public Infrastructure for insurance, promoting transparency and empowering policyholders. Here's all you need to know.

title: Why insurance sector is E-commerce firms' favourite poaching ground
description: Well-trained salesmen, with strong customer relations make the insurance sector prime target for e-commerce industry. They are wooing insurance workers with attractive bonuses, and flexible working hours.

title: Netizen says  ₹61 lakh cashless claim for  ₹2.40 crore policy rejected, Niva Bupa denies ‘baseless allegation’
description: A post has alleged that Niva Bupa denied  ₹61 lakh cashless claim for a cancer patient, despite a  ₹2.40 crore policy, while the company has denied the accusation, saying the pre-approved  ₹25 lakh is available to the family.&nbsp;

title: GST 2.0: Health insurance firms may raise policy tariffs by 3-5% to compensate for input tax credit losses amid tax cuts
description: GST 2.0: Health insurance firms may raise policy tariffs by 3-5% to offset their losses incurred from the input tax credit. Here's what industry experts think of this potential move, and how risky it is for the insurance sector.&nbsp;

title: GST rate cut on insurance: Should you wait till September 22 to buy new policy? Experts weigh in
description: As the central government cuts GST on individual life insurance policies from 18 per cent to nil, policyholders — new and old — are likely to benefit from September 22. Here's all you need to know.
